sentences: Revolving credit utilization is the most important driver of predicted default, with a strong effect that accounts for roughly 38% of the model's importance.
Risk rises steeply once utilization passes about 0.74, where the contribution to default log-odds reaches its highest level.
Past delinquencies are the second or third most important driver, with a moderate effect: having any past delinquency raises predicted risk compared with having none.
Income is also among the top three drivers, and higher income lowers predicted default risk, with the largest change at the low end of the income range.
Length of credit history has a weak to moderate effect, with longer histories associated with lower risk, although the data do not settle the exact size of this effect.
The effect of utilization is slightly larger when credit history is long, but the data do not settle whether this interaction is real at this sample size.
Debt-to-income ratio, number of dependents, months at address, age and recent credit inquiries each have a negligible effect on predicted default.
Utilization and debt-to-income ratio do not interact in any way that matters for the predictions.
